sections.h2: Where is the Town of East Hampton, and what does it include?
sections.html:
East Hampton is the easternmost town in New York, at the far end of Long Island's South Fork in Suffolk County. It takes in the village of East Hampton, part of the village of Sag Harbor, and the hamlets of Montauk, Amagansett, Wainscott, Springs, Northwest Harbor and Napeague. The town holds 74.33 square miles of land, stretches nearly 25 miles from Wainscott to Montauk Point, and has about 70 miles of shoreline. The town also has jurisdiction over Gardiners Island, one of the largest privately owned islands in the country.

That layout matters to a seller. Water borders the peninsula on the Atlantic side, Block Island Sound, Gardiners Bay and Napeague Bay, and the town includes eight state parks along the water, so a house in Montauk and a house in Springs reach very different buyers.

sections.h2: What shaped East Hampton's housing and economy?
sections.html:
English settlers arrived in the 1600s, and the town was organized under state law on March 7, 1788. Whaling out of nearby Sag Harbor, farming, and fishing came first. Montauk remains New York's largest fishing port, and summer crowds still drive much of the economy.

The Long Island Rail Road was extended to Montauk around 1880. Developers then built large summer estates, and later came smaller houses and bungalows, including prefabricated Leisurama homes at Culloden Point in the 1950s and 1960s. Former potato fields were turned into house lots. The town's own site lists community housing among its current programs.

sections.h2: How do East Hampton's Census numbers compare with the rest of New York?
sections.html:
QuickFacts estimates the town's mid-2025 population at 29,400, which is 3.7 percent above its 2020 base and well above the 21,457 counted in 2010. The profile is on the Census Bureau's site.

  • Owner-occupied housing: 77.8 percent
  • Typical value of a home its owner lives in (2020 to 2024 survey): $1,178,500
  • Typical household income: $132,348
  • Typical monthly rent: $2,578
  • Residents 65 and older: 23.2 percent
  • Residents born outside the United States: 23.2 percent

With a typical value above $1.1 million, many sales here pass the $1 million line where the state adds a residential tax for buyers, so price and closing figures deserve a careful look with your attorney.

sections.h2: Who bills East Hampton property taxes, and when do they come due?
sections.html:
The Receiver of Taxes prepares more than 24,000 bills and distributes the money to Suffolk County, the town, nine fire and fire protection districts, six school districts with five libraries and one museum district, five lighting districts, five road and water connection districts, and special use districts.

Source: East Hampton Assessor's Office, which also keeps ownership records, handles state exemptions and maintains the street address database used for E-911 dispatch. New STAR applicants must register with the state tax department to receive a STAR check. The 2025 to 2026 collection season ended on June 1, 2026, and the online payment portal closed for payments on June 2. Past that point, payments with penalties and interest go to the Suffolk County Comptroller in Riverhead, and the portal still lets you view and print bills and receipts.

sections.h2: Does East Hampton require an updated certificate of occupancy when a house sells?
sections.html:
Yes, the Town Code requires one on any change of ownership, with two exceptions. Under Chapter 102-14, no new certificate is needed if one was issued within six months before the transfer, or if the transfer only moves the property to a trust, LLC or similar entity for estate planning with the same beneficial owner.

The Town Board paused enforcement on March 10, 2026, and the pause runs retroactively from January 1, 2024 through December 31, 2026. The Building Department still processes applications, and its FAQ tells sellers to keep applying. It also says roughly six in ten applications involve improvements built without a permit, which lengthens review.

  • The updated certificate fee is $600.
  • Open building permits must be closed out, or renewal fees and violations can follow.
  • A closing in January 2027 or later falls after the stated end of the pause, so ask the department whether it will be extended.

sections.h2: How do East Hampton building applications and zoning limits work?
sections.html:
Every Building Department application must now be filed digitally through the town's OpenGov portal, and payments are made online, not at the counter. The department's notice of October 26, 2026 sets counter drop-off hours of 8:30 am to 3:30 pm on weekdays, with the first half hour reserved for licensed contractors and 9:00 to 10:30 am for the general public.

A zoning amendment effective July 1, 2025 limits gross floor area for a single-family residence to 7 percent of lot area plus 1,500 square feet or 10,000 square feet, whichever is less. Any building permit that includes clearing needs a staked survey showing the clearing envelope. If the house is rented, the town's rental registry requires a signed, notarized update form every time the tenancy changes.

sections.h2: What is the Community Preservation Fund tax on East Hampton sales?
sections.html:
The Peconic Bay Community Preservation Fund is financed by a 2 percent real estate transfer tax, created by Town Law 64-e in 1998 and administered under Tax Law section 31-d. A 2024 audit by the State Comptroller reported $127.2 million deposited during 2021 and 2022 and 2,352 acres of open space, farmland, parks and historic sites preserved through the end of 2022.

Ask your closing attorney whether the tax applies to your sale, which side pays it, and whether an exemption fits. State transfer tax of $2 per $500, the TP-584 return, and the extra 1 percent on residences at $1 million or more are described on the state tax department's page.

sections.h2: What are the practical ways to sell fast in East Hampton?
sections.html:
Sellers here choose between a public listing, a private sale and a cash purchase. A cash buyer is most useful when the house has an unresolved certificate of occupancy, postponed repairs or a tenant in place, since such buyers often take a property as it stands.

Begin with the permit file, any rental registry paperwork and the latest tax bills. If the house is rented, update the registry whenever the tenancy changes so the town's record matches who lives there. Then weigh a quick close against the higher price a full market sale might bring. Because the Building Department has a backlog, a sale that depends on a new certificate should leave room in the schedule.

faqs.q: Is East Hampton a town or a village?
faqs.a: Both exist. The Town of East Hampton is the large municipality of 74.33 square miles, and the incorporated village of East Hampton sits inside it, along with part of Sag Harbor and several hamlets.

faqs.q: What is the typical home value in East Hampton?
faqs.a: Roughly $1,178,500 for homes occupied by their owners, per the Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 survey. Household income in the middle of the range is $132,348.

faqs.q: Do I need an updated certificate of occupancy to sell in East Hampton?
faqs.a: The code requires one when ownership changes, though enforcement is paused through December 31, 2026. The Building Department still takes applications, charges $600, and advises sellers to apply.

faqs.q: When is Grievance Day in East Hampton?
faqs.a: In 2026 it was May 19, and the Assessor's calendar sets it on the third Tuesday in May. The tentative roll is posted May 1, and the final roll arrives July 1.

faqs.q: Who do I pay if I missed the East Hampton tax deadline?
faqs.a: After June 1 the Town no longer accepts payment. Late payments, with penalties and interest, go to the Suffolk County Comptroller, and the town recommends certified mail with your tax map number.
